title: Knowledge Check 5: Lessons 21-25
description: Questions pooled from Lessons 21-25 of the ai-adoption series. Score 80% or higher to progress toward the practice exam.

questions.question: A model generates a risk score about a customer. Why does that score count as personal data?
options: It is personal data only if the person supplied the underlying facts
It relates to an identifiable person and can affect that person
It is personal data only when it is stored with the person's name
It counts only if a regulator has reviewed the model behind it
questions.explanation: The test is identifiability and effect, not who supplied the input, so inferences a tool produces about people sit inside the same rules as the data it consumed.

questions.question: A screening model ranks applicants and a reviewer approves the shortlist unchanged. What has failed?
options: Nothing, because a human did look at the list before it was used
The documentation requirement, because no log of the review was kept
The human review safeguard, since a stamp cannot change the outcome
The notice requirement, because applicants were not told a model was used
questions.explanation: A safeguard exists so a person can genuinely reject the machine's call; a reviewer who lacks the authority or practice of overriding it leaves the decision effectively automated.

questions.question: Your team feeds personal data into a third-party tool. Who does privacy law hold responsible?
options: The vendor, because it operates the model and the servers on your behalf
Both parties equally, with legal duties split evenly between them
Neither, once a data processing agreement is signed by both sides
The organization deciding to process it, which stays accountable
questions.explanation: A vendor agreement allocates blame between the parties, but the party that decides why and how personal data is used keeps the accountability.

questions.question: What separates a near miss from an incident, and why does it matter?
options: It caused no harm, and it flags where the next failure is likely
It caused limited harm, and it must be reported to a regulator
It is a vendor failure, and logging it belongs to the vendor
It is a false alarm, and it can be safely ignored once it is found
questions.explanation: A near miss is a harm that was caught before it landed, which makes it the cheapest evidence you will ever get about where a real failure is forming.

questions.question: An incident is confirmed. What is the first job?
options: Find the root cause so the fix can be designed before anything else
Notify every affected customer before any internal step is taken
Stop the harm from spreading, then work out why it happened
Document the timeline in full detail for the post-incident review
questions.explanation: Containment comes before diagnosis because the damage keeps accruing while you investigate; understanding the cause can wait until the bleeding has stopped.

questions.question: What shows that remediation worked, rather than that the symptom merely stopped?
options: The immediate problem has stopped and no complaint has arrived
The same failure could not happen again through the same path
The vendor has confirmed the model was updated to a newer one
The post-incident review document has been written and filed
questions.explanation: Fixing the root cause, or adding a check that catches that class of error, is what prevents a repeat; a quiet week only means nobody has noticed yet.

questions.question: How does provider risk differ from model risk?
options: Model risk is about price, while provider risk is about licensing terms
Model risk disappears once a newer model is released by the same provider
A model can be swapped, but a provider outage defeats any replacement
Provider risk ends when the contract names a fixed model version
questions.explanation: A model is replaceable in principle, but when the company serving it goes down, changes terms, or exits, no substitute model rescues you at that layer.

questions.question: Why test an alternative provider on a regular schedule instead of waiting for a forced switch?
options: Because a tested alternative shows what a switch would cost
Because providers require proof of an alternative before renewal
Because testing resets the notice period on model retirement
Because alternatives are cheaper once a contract has been signed
questions.explanation: Periodic testing turns an unthinkable move into a sized one, which is what gives you leverage when a price or a model changes on short notice.

questions.question: What does keeping your AI work portable mean in practice?
options: Store outputs wherever the provider's interface keeps them
Keep prompts and outputs in formats you control and can export
Rely on the provider to migrate your data if it retires a model
Copy everything to a second provider every month to stay current
questions.explanation: Portability lives in the artifacts you would have to move: prompts written to travel, and outputs saved in a standard format somewhere you control.

questions.question: Why does a clause saying you own the output not guarantee you can stop a competitor copying it?
options: Because a contract can assign rights but cannot create a copyright
Because ownership clauses only apply to works registered with the office
Because vendors keep ownership of anything their models produce
Because copyright protects ideas rather than the expression of them
questions.explanation: A contract can only pass along rights the provider actually holds; where no human authored the expression, there is no copyright for the clause to hand over.

questions.question: Which term matters most before routing confidential material through an AI tool?
options: The limit on the vendor's total liability across the contract term
The notice period the vendor must give before retiring a model
Whether the vendor may train on your inputs and outputs
The support hours, the escalation path, and the named contact
questions.explanation: If the vendor may train on what you send, confidential material can end up inside a model later served to other customers, so this term decides most of the data-side risk.

questions.question: Why can typing a proprietary process into a tool that trains on customer data destroy a trade secret?
options: Because the tool will resell the process as a standalone product
Because a trade secret survives only while it stays secret
Because the vendor becomes the legal owner of the process once sent
Because copyright in the process transfers to the model provider
questions.explanation: Trade secret status depends on secrecy, so once the material is absorbed into a model that serves others, the protection can be gone even without any single act of copying.

questions.question: An agent differs from a fixed automation mainly because it:
options: chooses its own steps toward a goal instead of running a written sequence
runs each step faster by using a newer and larger underlying model
records every action it takes so a person can review the complete history later
starts on a schedule without any person triggering the first step
questions.explanation: Automation follows steps written in advance, so its behavior can be predicted; an agent decides the path itself, which is why not every action can be foreseen.

questions.question: Why must a guardrail be deterministic when the model it constrains is probabilistic?
options: Because deterministic controls are cheaper to build than controls that depend on the model
Because a control that relies on the model behaving well can fail whenever the model is wrong
Because deterministic controls remove the need for any person to own the outcome of a run
Because probabilistic controls cannot be written in a language that non-engineers can easily understand
questions.explanation: The model predicts and is sometimes confidently wrong, so a rule that only asks it to behave is a wish; a real guardrail blocks prohibited actions regardless of what the model produces.

questions.question: A support agent is locked to the correct inbox and refund tool, yet it still drafts a poor reply. What does this show?
options: That guardrails guarantee accuracy only when all five families are fully deployed
That guardrails eliminate the need for monitoring once the boundary has been tested
That guardrails bound where a system acts but do not make its work inside that bound correct
That guardrails prevent bad output from reaching a customer without any human being in the path
questions.explanation: Guardrails bound the blast radius and make failures reversible and traceable; they do not make the model accurate inside its lane, which is a separate quality problem.
